Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific context, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This approach demonstrates how transfer learning can efficiently adapt general genomic models to specific tissues without de novo training.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and immunotherapeutic features. The work is exploratory and the abstract is truncated, so the strength of the clinical claims cannot be fully assessed.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

This study identifies cellular senescence-associated prognostic signals in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) by screening across cancers and integrating multi-omics and pathological data. The authors build a senescence-based risk stratification model that links molecular features to the tumor microenvironment and potential clinical outcomes. The work aims to connect senescence biology with translational risk assessment in BLCA.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, reducing the tedium and error-proneness of library design, and can also be used in silico to analyze genomic AI models.

Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.

This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive power of these epigenetic marks as biomarkers for male fertility in dairy cattle. The work represents an initial step toward developing operational tools for fertility prediction based on sperm DNA methylation.

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab, a free community-driven web platform that bundles over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of microbial omics data (metabarcoding, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics). It lowers computational and technical barriers for microbiologists by providing accessible, standardized pipelines without requiring local infrastructure or coding expertise.

Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) 2026-Oct-29 Medium

Verix: a toolkit for benchmarking and harmonization of complex structural variants.

Verix is a new software toolkit that benchmarks and harmonizes complex structural variants (CSVs), which are large genomic rearrangements involving multiple breakpoints. Existing evaluation tools only handle simple single-breakpoint variants, so Verix fills a gap by quantifying how accurately methods reconstruct multi-breakpoint CSV events and by distinguishing different types of reconstruction errors. This enables more systematic development and comparison of CSV detection methods.

MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

MitImpact 4 expands mitochondrial variant interpretation from the 13 protein-coding genes to the entire mitochondrial genome, covering all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants including tRNA and rRNA genes. This addresses a diagnostic blind spot where pathogenic variants in RNA genes were poorly served by existing predictors, providing functional consequences for the full genome.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

This study re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 and 9 shared across cell lines. The authors then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and applied their findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. The work provides an experimental benchmark for evaluating computational predictions of regulatory non-coding variants at cancer risk loci.

Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.

The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum-derived cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched individuals with pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease versus non-AD controls. They detected altered methylation features in blood cfDNA, including brain-specific epigenetic signatures, suggesting that cfDNA methylomes can capture AD-related changes non-invasively.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated computational framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis into a single seamless pipeline, reducing manual intervention across heterogeneous platforms.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across diverse tissues and disease states. This reference-free approach reveals disease-relevant isoform changes that conventional annotation-based methods miss.

Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.

This study shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment can mimic the effects of stiffness on cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates develop stiffness-like traits, including increased cell stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through narrow constrictions, and these changes are linked to epigenomic and transcriptomic remodeling via cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling. The work suggests that viscous cues, not just elastic rigidity, help encode metastatic behavior.

Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.

This paper shows that commonly used computational variant effect predictors are biased by ancestry because their training data under-represent global populations. By combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free predictors, the authors improve variant classification in hereditary cancer genes across ancestries, offering a more equitable approach to variant interpretation.

Bivalent Inhibitor Development for a Dynamic Epigenetic Tandem Reader Protein Using a Combinatorial Histone Code.

This preprint describes the design of bivalent inhibitors targeting BPTF, an epigenetic reader protein that contains a PHD finger and tandem bromodomains. By using a combinatorial histone code approach, the authors aim to develop chemical probes that simultaneously engage multiple reader domains, which could improve selectivity and potency for this dynamic epigenetic target. The work provides a framework for targeting tandem reader proteins in drug discovery.

Same-cell mapping of epigenetic regulatory state to functional proteomic output.

The authors present Proteo-Seq, a single-cell method that simultaneously profiles chromatin accessibility from intact nuclei and cytoplasmic protein output from the same cell. The device uses a two-layer microwell stack with a dissolvable gel trapdoor to route cytoplasmic proteins to targeted or discovery proteomics while nuclei are transferred for snATAC-seq. This enables direct same-cell mapping of epigenetic regulatory state to functional proteomic output.

Nanopore Sequencing for Epigenetic Decoding: Applications, Analytical Constraints, and Translational Prospects.

This review examines how nanopore sequencing can decode multiple epigenetic layers—DNA and RNA modifications, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility—from long native molecules, rather than assaying each separately. It surveys current applications, discusses analytical constraints and limitations, and outlines translational prospects for clinical and research use.

This study demonstrates a nanopore-based forensic profiling approach that simultaneously analyzes STRs, InDels, SNPs, and mtDNA in long reads to support both identity matching and appearance prediction. Translational oncology 2026-Oct-16 Medium

Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.

This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where clonal hematopoiesis and treatment effects complicate variant interpretation. The authors find that direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies remain retrospective and internally validated, limiting clinical translation. They outline current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions for these epigenomic and fragmentomic approaches.

Single-cell variant landscape of the human mitochondrial genome reveals cell type-specific functions and disease mechanisms.

The authors present scMOCHA, a scalable computational framework that detects high-confidence mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy at single-cell resolution directly from standard scRNA-seq data. Applying it to public human PBMC datasets, they uncover cell type-specific patterns of mtDNA variants, linking heteroplasmy to cell-type functions and disease mechanisms. This work establishes a new way to mine existing single-cell transcriptomic data for mitochondrial genetic diversity.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.

This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl histone modification, as a key epigenetic regulator of long-term spatial memory. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, and Kcr appears to act as a molecular switch controlling glutamatergic neurotransmission underlying memory consolidation. The work extends epigenetic control of memory beyond the well-studied histone acetylation to a different acyl modification.

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under Mendelian randomization, while accounting for high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographics. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, and this work aims to robustly handle them to improve causal network inference in genomic trio data.

XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.

XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) DNA methylation microarray data. This addresses a common problem where mouse stromal cells contaminate human tumor samples in PDX models, which can confound epigenetic analyses. The tool enables researchers to quantify and account for this contamination directly from existing methylation data.

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by matching degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap in mobile genetic element analysis for staphylococci.

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tested whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors found that prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are universally reliable.

ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
